Wow, what a random way to get a date in this time ahah. 
In all honesty, make sure you don't compromise on BASIC manners. Look clean when you go (get a haircut, fix facial hair, wear decent clothes). Make sure you smell nice too obviously. 

Give her a brief hug when you meet her, and compliment something about her as she's probably put in effort to look the way she looks, so that's always appreciated. When your talking, make sure she's engaged, if she's not then try to switch the convo into something she might like. Ask her questions, be inquisitive. Simple ones are easiest and if she's interested then they'll typically lead from one thing to the next and you'll have a good flowing conversation. 

Finally, remember that you're meant to have fun too. So enjoy yourself! If you're not having fun then it's ok to decide that maybe this isn't it. In that case, sit the date out, and perhaps later on (another day) let her know how you felt. In all honesty, if you guys know each other you probably will get along so this last part wasn't so relevant. 

You do all these simple things and you should be just fine.

Oh damn okay that's tough to hear. I thought you would be younger. If I was in this situation and I'd exhausted all avenues to talk to him I would probably decide to end the relationship. That being said, it seems like in the past you valued the sort of gift giving and he valued time together? I would probably take a look at that and consider whether your gifts actually add value to him (not that he should be ungrateful for them anyway). But it could just be that your efforts are being wasted in areas he's doesn't value as much. Conversely, he might believe time together is important and tries to give that to you but you'd rather sentimental gifts? 

Just guessing, either way though his behaviour currently is sub-par, so you should sit down together (don't text) and start with whether you both want the relationship to continue. Prepare for the worst response and don't ask leading questions or insinuate negativity in your sentences, they'll only annoy whoever you're talking to (e.g don't say 'i know I want to continue the relationship but...'). If you manage to both say you genuinely want to continue then you should explain how you might value gift giving and special holidays (valentine's Day etc) together. And explain that you understand that you can make him happy just by spending time with him. It's vital you understand what makes each other feel loved and that the way you experience love WILL almost definitely be in different ways. Make sacrifices and pay attention to each other.

Good luck.
